html:
The Bengali Language Movement was a campaign in East Pakistan, now Bangladesh, for Bengali to be an official language of Pakistan. Its turning point came on 21 February 1952, when police in Dhaka shot dead students who were protesting.

Bengali speakers were the majority of Pakistan's people, but its leaders wanted Urdu alone as the state language. In 1948 Jinnah said so in a speech in Dhaka, to protests from students. In 1952 the government restated it. Students at the University of Dhaka defied a ban on gatherings, and police opened fire. Several were killed, among them Abul Barkat and Rafiquddin Ahmed.

The deaths turned the movement into a mass cause. A memorial, the Shaheed Minar, was raised where they fell. In 1956 Pakistan's constitution made Bengali an official language alongside Urdu.

The movement was the first great sign that East and West Pakistan were drifting apart. Young activists such as Sheikh Mujibur Rahman went on to lead the fight for self rule that ended in the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971. In 1999 UNESCO declared 21 February International Mother Language Day.
sum: The Bengali Language Movement was a campaign in East Pakistan, now Bangladesh, for Bengali to be an official language of Pakistan. Its turning point came on 21 February 1952, when police in Dhaka shot dead students who were protesting.
